title: There are Levels to It: Red Teaming LLMs with Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
claim: Attacks succeed through adaptive multi-turn interaction: a high-level strategy guides utterances, switching strategy after failure until a harmful response emerges.
layout: Single vertical flow, two turns, policy boxes left, dialogue right, dashed turn boundary
description: A worked example of one two-turn adversarial conversation. At the top right, a gray dotted box holds a HarmBench prompt asking how to make a fake ID. On the left, inside a red dashed outline, orange High Level Policy boxes state a strategy (turn 1: roleplay a tourist; turn 2: ask for instructions). Each feeds a Low Level Policy box that generates an utterance. On the right, pink utterance boxes alternate with blue Target LLM boxes and their light-blue responses. Curved dark-blue arrows connect the left and right columns. In turn 1 the response is benign, marked with a red X and 'Use different strategy'. In turn 2 the response is harmful, marked with a check mark at bottom left.
caption: An adversarial conversation between the red team agent and the target LLM. The dialogue state consists of alternating Target and Low-Level Policy utterances.
abstract: Red teaming is essential for securing Large Language Models, yet current automated methods remain limited by templates and single-turn attacks. To simulate the complex, interactive nature of real-world adversarial attacks, we introduce a novel red teaming paradigm designed to maximize expected cumulative harm through strategic interaction. By formalizing red teaming as a Markov Decision Process in a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, we navigate the challenges of sparse rewards and long-horizon planning. Our generative agent learns diverse, multi-turn attacks using a token-level harm reward, consistently uncovering vulnerabilities that bypass baselines. This approach achieves a new state of the art and reframes LLM red teaming as a principled, trajectory-based process.
